entry_points.text: Aux granularity query is an inline leaf returning a fixed resolution usable without kernel entry.
Probe returns silent low lines after quiescing; affinity construction builds per-vector masks and setting applies them with notification.
Chip entries activate and start with optional resend or unmask; domain entries activate parent-first once and tear down parent-last.
Resend replays pending except on level lines; collection finalizes probe masks and nested entry runs threads outside the lock.

exports.text: Expiry queues offer empty-safe minimum peek, node and head init, membership test, first/next/previous traversal and delete reporting prior presence; relies on external tree helpers.
Clock access offers inline capture plus validate for readers and paired invalidate plus revalidate for writers, with single and dual clock forms.
Diagnostics offer symbolic decoders for timer flags, clock identities, soft interrupt classes and tick dependency causes, each with definition and value forms.
Affinity setup keeps per-CPU lines fixed else selects online targets preferring current choice with NUMA fallback; chip, trigger type and MSI links are assigned per line.

hazards.text: Peek returns null when empty; uninitialized links can falsely look queued, coarse/raw/aux stores must not be confused, and readonly status plus leap codes are observed state.
Affinity and startup fail safe with null, zero vectors or abort on no online CPU; probing filters spurious activity and warns when effective affinity stays empty via external warning helpers.
Chained lines must never reach threaded handlers and warn when they do; migrating high-rate edge lines busy-wait for progress rather than pending forever.

invariants.text: Discipline selects adjustments by mode bits, reports PLL and leap state by status with fixed sync codes, and uses fixed decimal scales with tick from HZ.
Namespace clocks are identified by mode and report contention rather than spin; aux granularity is fixed and offsets pair signed seconds with nanos.

Vector sets honour reservations and spread middle vectors, failing null when infeasible; programming narrows managed masks, defers or pends busy moves, and stores early hierarchy requests, using external mask, alloc, scheduling, per-CPU and utility helpers.

Startup aborts without online affinity and orders chip versus affinity by flags; hierarchy is parent-first with rollback, disable is idempotent, retrigger prefers chip then ancestors and nested resend redirects to parent.
Trigger narrows to sense bits with masking when required; MSI records entry and base line, and accounting bumps per-CPU and totals.
Descriptor lookup uses sparse tree or bounded flat table with null on miss; one build warns when effective affinity stays empty after programming.

locks.text: Classic timers carry an optional lock-validation map; shared clocks use odd-even versions with acquire on read and release around writes, no sleepable lock, with external barriers.
Autoprobe holds a dedicated external mutex across detection with per-descriptor spinlocks; public affinity resolves the line then holds its spinlock while applying updates.
Notify needs descriptor lock with extra reference; temp masks use a static lock, resend queueing holds its lock briefly, and progress wait releases the descriptor lock while spinning.
Line setters run under descriptor or bus scope; sparse insertion serializes on a mutex and proc width tracking on its own raw lock.

state_machines.text: Queue nodes start detached after init, become queued on insert and return to detached on remove, with queued inferred from non-empty link.
Lines move among disabled, masked and started; enable and startup clear prior marks and set started, shutdown clears resend and started while marking disabled.
Candidates arm then drop on spurious activity or failed activation; collection shuts down probed lines and reports a low-line mask or single firer.
Trigger commits on acceptance; managed startup preserves depth, wakeup lines divert to power handling, and dispatch needs power permission plus enabled actions.

structs.text: Classic timer holds expiry tick, placement link, self callback and flags; ordered queues key tree nodes by expiry with cached minimum and linked variants for traversal.
User time pairs seconds with subseconds in legacy and modern forms plus tick counts; control block orders mode, offset, frequency, errors, status, PPS and TAI.
Shared page holds versioned clocks with mode, cycle, mask, multiplier and stamps overlaid by namespace offsets, plus coarse, raw, aux bases and a generation-counted random area.
Clocks are small integers with aux range above bases; timer files use absolute and cancel bits, and startup distinguishes normal, managed and abort.
A prebuilt chained action warns when misused; interrupt state lives in one field with helpers setting started, masked, activated and pending bits via external bit helpers.
